summary: Morongo Transmission LLC, a non-load-serving CAISO Participating Transmission Owner, answers the show cause order. It says its tariff needs no amendment and that it will stay in the proceeding as a party.
ask: Find that the Morongo Tariff is just and reasonable and needs no amendment; Morongo will make compliance filings if FERC directs residual changes.

points.point: Morongo Transmission has no end-use customers, so the load interconnection reforms do not reach its tariff.
points.quote: Morongo Transmission LLC is a Non-Load-Serving Participating [Transmission Owner] and has no End-Use Customers.

points.point: Morongo holds a 30-year lease of part of the transfer capability of SCE's West of Devers facilities.
points.quote: Morongo Transmission holds a 30-year lease of a portion of the transfer capability of Southern California Edison Company’s (“SCE”) upgraded West of Devers transmission facilities

points.point: The Morongo Tariff defers its load interconnection sections (Sections 8 to 10) to SCE's TO Tariff, so SCE's reforms would cover them.
points.quote: SCE could implement those reforms to its own tariff without Morongo Transmission needing to take further action to amend the Morongo Tariff.

points.point: Morongo offers compliance filings if FERC finds residual changes are needed.
points.quote: to the extent that the Commission determines any residual or conforming amendments are required to the Morongo Tariff, Morongo Transmission will make compliance filings as directed.

points.point: Morongo stays a party because resource adequacy and large load interconnection matter to the Tribe.
points.quote: Morongo Transmission nevertheless intends to continue participating as a party in this proceeding

throughLine.text: Answers the E-10 CAISO show cause order, which named every Participating Transmission Owner as respondent, by arguing that a non-load-serving owner with no end-use customers needs no tariff change.
